sections.label: The opening
sections.line: How we stopped a hundred agents at Web Summit: pausing took seconds, hearing the order up to an hour.
sections.para: The Big Stop, the hand brake, the final hold, and what got through.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The order; seconds to pause; up to an hour to hear; 80 to 94% fewer wakes; two file stops; leaks; the lesson.

sections.label: Part six of ten days
sections.line: Part six of ten days at Web Summit, after the Mac bottleneck.

sections.label: The order
sections.line: Stop all work unless critical, until we realign; each person may restart their own agents.

sections.label: Pausing took seconds
sections.line: Conductors paused 6 and 12 scheduled agents in one to four seconds, pausing not deleting.
sections.para: The order went on every board by 23:40.

sections.label: Hearing it took up to an hour
sections.line: Each conductor heard the order at its next wake: 5, 11, 19 and 33 minutes; Silvio's 2 h 36, waiting for his word.

sections.label: What it saved
sections.line: Scheduled wakes fell about 80%, 94% and 91% on three accounts; some agents were kept or restarted.

sections.label: Three stops
sections.line: A hand brake at 15:15 and a final hold at 18:12 on 12 November, both files, lifted on 13 November.

sections.label: What got through
sections.line: Tasks a session could not pause, agents that never read the hold, two small commits, things not ours.
sections.para: Found by the records and a reviewer agent.

sections.label: A stop is a file
sections.line: A stop is a file read first, a path into every account, a switch a person reaches, pause not delete, check after.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not every account reported; wakes not tokens; a hundred is one account; times from the conductors' records.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The Web Summit team repository's stop reports, hold commits, automation notes and reviews.
